app_purpose: Java network application framework (TCP/IP transport layer). Apps using ObjectSerializationCodecFactory / ObjectSerializationDecoder decode Java-native-serialized objects off the wire via org.apache.mina.core.buffer.AbstractIoBuffer#getObject(ClassLoader). After CVE-2024-52046 the decoder is default-deny: the app must accept(...) the classes it legitimately deserializes (acceptMatchers / ClassNameMatcher allowlist).
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data guarded by an allowlist that is APPLIED TOO LATE (CWE-502). CVE-2024-52046 added the acceptMatchers class allowlist (default-deny) to AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() and enforced it in resolveClass(). But the decoder's inner ObjectInputStream.readClassDescriptor() runs FIRST, and for a Serializable class (MINA type-1 descriptor) it calls Class.forName(className, /* initialize */ true, classLoader) BEFORE the allowlist is ever consulted. Merely resolving a class name off the wire therefore RUNS that class's STATIC INITIALIZER, even for a non-allowlisted class that resolveClass() then rejects. A class whose observable side effect lives in a static initializer fires before the guard blocks the deserialization. CVE-2026-42778 closes this in 2.1.12/2.2.7 by hoisting the acceptMatchers check ahead of Class.forName in readClassDescriptor() (and resolveClass()), so a non-allowlisted class is rejected before initialization.
external_trigger_note: Apache MINA is a NETWORK framework, not an HTTP app: its real entry point is a TCP server. The trigger is a REAL EXTERNAL network trigger -- a separate `client` container (app/Client.java) connects over TCP across the docker network to a REAL MINA NioSocketAcceptor + ProtocolCodecFilter(ObjectSerializationCodecFactory) server (app/Server.java) and writes the crafted length-prefixed MINA serialized stream. The server's REAL, unmodified published mina-core decoder (doDecode -> in.setMatchers(acceptMatchers) -> in.getObject(classLoader)) deserializes it through the real allowlist. Not HTTP, but a genuine external TCP network trigger, exactly how MINA is used in production and satisfying the external-trigger requirement for a network framework. Nothing is deserialized in-process by a test harness.

flag.resource: the class-deserialization allowlist (acceptMatchers/ClassNameMatcher, default-deny) that CVE-2024-52046 added to AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() to keep untrusted classes from being deserialized/loaded/initialized; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir that only code loaded/run past that guard can read
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) in the SERVER container at start. Two DISTINCT server-side side-channels read it during getObject(): (1) the readObject channel -- PcbSeed.readObject() reads it into a transient `flag` field during FULL reconstruction, echoed by the server's messageReceived as 'PCB_READOBJECT=<flag>'; (2) the static-init channel -- PcbCanary's STATIC INITIALIZER reads it into the shared Beacon when the class is resolved (Class.forName(name,true)), echoed by the server's exceptionCaught (the class is then rejected by the allowlist) as 'PCB_STATICINIT=<flag>'. Absent from MINA source, Server.java, Client.java. The external client NEVER holds the canary: the serialized stream it sends carries only class name + descriptor (PcbSeed.flag is transient; PcbCanary has no fields).
flag.detect: the external `client` container sends a normal MINA type-1 stream (mode=seed|canary|expected) over TCP to the REAL running MINA server; the version's own unmodified readClassDescriptor()/resolveClass() ordering decides whether readObject runs (seed) or the static initializer runs (canary) before the allowlist rejects the class -> the flag token is echoed back over TCP and appears in the client's received bytes iff it did. Each class has exactly ONE flag channel, so a single ${PCB_FLAG} token distinguishes readObject (seed) from static-init (canary).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2026-42778 (Apache advisory): 'The fix for CVE-2024-52046 in Apache MINA AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() was incomplete. The classname allowlist of classes allowed to be deserialized was applied too late after a static initializer in a class to be read might already have been executed.' CVE-2024-52046 (CVSS 10.0): the ObjectSerializationDecoder lacked deserialization defenses; its fix (2.0.27/2.1.10/2.2.4) added the acceptMatchers/ClassNameMatcher allowlist (accept(Class...)/accept(Pattern)/accept(String...)), default-deny, enforced in resolveClass(). CVE-2026-42778 fixed in 2.1.12/2.2.7 by applying the allowlist BEFORE Class.forName in readClassDescriptor(). SOURCE-VERIFIED from Maven Central sources jars: 2.2.3 has no allowlist; 2.2.4 readClassDescriptor() type-1 calls Class.forName(name,true) before resolveClass()'s acceptMatchers check; 2.2.7 checks acceptMatchers before Class.forName.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 as REAL-SERVER-TCP (hard policy: the prior in-process Driver.getObject() trigger was BANNED). Apache MINA is a NETWORK framework, so each version now runs a REAL MINA NioSocketAcceptor TCP server (app/Server.java) with ProtocolCodecFilter(new ObjectSerializationCodecFactory()) and the acceptMatchers allowlist configured (via reflection, so one source compiles on V0=2.2.3 which predates the accept() API) to accept ONLY the legit class PcbExpected -- NOT PcbSeed/PcbCanary. A SEPARATE `client` container (app/Client.java) connects over TCP across the docker network and writes the crafted length-prefixed MINA serialized stream; the server's REAL, unmodified published mina-core decoder path (ObjectSerializationDecoder.doDecode -> in.setMatchers(acceptMatchers) -> AbstractIoBuffer.getObject(ClassLoader)) deserializes it through the real allowlist. Genuine EXTERNAL network trigger (real TCP, separate process/container) -- the way MINA is actually used; not HTTP but a real network entry point. No MINA code edited. Runtime = maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-11, REAL Maven Central mina-core 2.2.3/2.2.4/2.2.7. Variant A (same running sink getObject(); same rce-oob canary file /canary/flag.txt; the differential is WHICH benign canary class is sent -> WHICH side-channel surfaces the flag). PcbSeed reads the canary only in readObject() (full-reconstruction channel); PcbCanary reads it only in a STATIC INITIALIZER (class-resolution channel). Each class has exactly ONE flag channel, so a single ${PCB_FLAG} token tells readObject from static-init: seed's server response can carry the flag only via PCB_READOBJECT, canary's only via PCB_STATICINIT (echoed from the shared Beacon by the server's exceptionCaught when the class is then rejected). GUARD lineage source-verified from upstream sources jars (AbstractIoBuffer.getObject inner ObjectInputStream): V0=2.2.3 has NO allowlist (resolveClass else-branch returns any class); V1=2.2.4 has the CVE-2024-52046 acceptMatchers allowlist in resolveClass() BUT readClassDescriptor()'s type-1 path runs Class.forName(name, /*initialize*/ true, cl) BEFORE it -> static initializer of a rejected class STILL fires; V2=2.2.7 is the CVE-2026-42778 fix -- readClassDescriptor() applies acceptMatchers 'BEFORE calling Class.forName' (and resolveClass() 'before any Class.forName() call'). BENIGN benchmark canary (rce-oob): PcbSeed.readObject / PcbCanary static init only READ /canary/flag.txt and echo the per-run token; PcbSeed.flag is transient (never on the wire); no gadget chain, no JNDI/RMI, no command execution. The client generates the MINA streams itself at runtime (pure java.io, no canary present in the client container), so they carry only class name + descriptor + empty field data, never the flag. RUNTIME REPRODUCED over real external TCP (flag=PCBFLAG_6e26e87fa038cfdda7dc8ca827077465): original(PcbSeed seed)@v0 -> server echoes PCB_MSG class=PcbSeed PCB_READOBJECT=<flag> (reaches; no accept() API); original(seed)@v1 -> PCB_ERR ClassNotFoundException:null PCB_STATICINIT= (BLOCKED: allowlist rejects in resolveClass, readObject never runs, PcbSeed has no static flag); expected(PcbExpected)@v1 -> PCB_MSG class=PcbExpected (allowlist is LIVE, not deny-all); bypass(PcbCanary canary)@v1 -> PCB_ERR ClassNotFoundException:null PCB_STATICINIT=<flag> (RESIDUAL REACHES: the class is rejected by the allowlist BUT its static initializer already ran during Class.forName(name,true) and leaked the flag -- empirically confirming 'allowlist applied too late'); bypass(canary)@v2 -> PCB_ERR ClassNotFoundException:Class not in accept list PcbCanary PCB_STATICINIT= (BLOCKED: rejected before Class.forName, static init never ran); original(seed)@v2 -> Class not in accept list PcbSeed (BLOCKED). KEY: on the SAME v1 (2.2.4) server, PcbSeed's readObject flag is BLOCKED (PCB_READOBJECT empty) while PcbCanary's static-init flag FIRES (PCB_STATICINIT=<flag>) -- the two side-channels behave differently, directly demonstrating that on 2.2.4 the static initializer runs before the allowlist rejects but readObject does not. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct releases (2.2.3->2.2.4->2.2.7); distinct fixed_version for each CVE (2.2.4 vs 2.2.7); V1 genuinely has the -52046 guard (readObject seed IS rejected, PcbExpected accepted) and is genuinely bypassed by the static-init residual it does not cover; V2 closes exactly that residual; original(readObject) != residual(static-init) on V1; V1 does NOT block the residual (2.2.4 does not already check before Class.forName).
